input: Map out a sensory-friendly travel kit for my child

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The type of travel (flight, road trip, train) drastically changes which sensory challenges arise and which items are most useful.
The child's age and specific sensory profile (sensitivities vs. seeking behaviours, any diagnosis) determines which categories of items to include or avoid.
Trip duration and destination environment affect how comprehensive and portable the kit needs to be.
Budget and carry-on/packing restrictions (e.g., TSA rules for flights) limit what can realistically go in the kit.
The child's known calming preferences (tactile, auditory, visual, oral motor) should drive which sensory tools are prioritised.
Knowing whether the goal is a quick reference checklist, a fully sourced shopping list, or a packed bag changes the format and depth of the output.
Whether items need to be bought new, sourced from what is already at home, or DIY-assembled affects the recommended next steps.

gold.taskTitle: Build a sensory-friendly travel kit for your child
gold.taskDescription: Create a tailored, sensory-friendly travel kit with the right items to keep the child comfortable and regulated during trips.

questions.title: What type of travel is this kit mainly for?
questions.description: Identify the primary mode of travel — e.g., long-haul flight, road trip, train journey — to tailor sensory challenges and item choices accordingly.

questions.title: How old is your child, and what is their sensory profile?
questions.description: Understand the child's age and whether they are primarily sensory-sensitive, sensory-seeking, or have a specific diagnosis like autism or SPD.

questions.title: How long will the typical trip or journey be?
questions.description: Determine trip duration to gauge how many items, how much variety, and how much bulk the kit needs to handle extended time.

questions.title: What is your budget for putting this kit together?
questions.description: Establish a spending range so recommendations stay realistic — from a low-cost DIY kit to a fully stocked premium set.

questions.title: Which sensory inputs calm your child most reliably?
questions.description: Identify whether the child responds best to tactile tools, sound dampening, visual focus aids, oral motor items, or movement/proprioceptive input.

questions.title: Do you need a checklist, a shopping list, or a full packing guide?
questions.description: Clarify the desired output format so the plan matches how the parent intends to use it — quick reference vs. step-by-step assembly guide.

questions.title: Will you buy new items or use things you already own?
questions.description: Determine whether the plan should recommend specific products to purchase, help repurpose existing household items, or a mix of both.
